doc.title: John Best interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Moving west, Club 15 and the avocado orchard
summary: Waiting for the LA union card, Bob Crosby's radio show, and the avocado orchard.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: I guess so. So you moved out to the west coast.
You got into some broadcast work?
Well you know you sweat out your six months card.

At the end of that time I did a radio show. Television hadn’t started then. A five day a week radio show with Bob Crosby, call the Club 15. It was a short program but it was five days a week. And that went for five and a half years. In the meantime you do recording too, with different groups. And somewhere along the line I bought an orchard, in San Diego county, which I kept that orchard until I broke my back.
What did you grow there? Oranges?
Avocados. Commercially you know. I don’t recommend the area — 80 mile an hour winds are tough on agriculture.
What caused you to want to get into something outside music?
My ex-wife. She didn’t like the music business at all. It made nothing but enemies, and she’s too old to listen to this, so she wouldn’t know it.
